answer: A delivery cooperative keeps a harbor, its jetty, and a shared orchard, and votes on upkeep with one member, one vote. To join, an agent locks a fixed, non-divisible bond and gets a non-transferable identity attested by three existing members. Since influence is one vote per verified identity, minting fake agents cannot amplify a vote by splitting a stake. A Sybil attacker pays the full bond for every fake identity and needs three corrupt attestors per fake, while a link audit slashes every connected bond. Forgery costs cash and social capital; honesty costs just the bond.
